text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Deficit target at risk after June budget deficit of 3.1 billion shekels.
- Authorities looking for Israeli businessman who went missing in West Bank.
- Netanyahu to meet Levy today; ready to dissolve his "kitchen cabinet".
- Defence Minister Mordechai demands to know who is responsible for fire at Arrow missile plant four months ago.
JERUSALEM POST
- Hebron pipe bomb wounds two soldiers.
- Israeli army condemns Palestinian Authority's reluctance to fight Hebron violence.
- Israeli army doctor saves life of Palestinian boy.
- Government: Applications for 1997 investment aid down sharply.
- Arison bids three billion shekels for 34.5 percent stake in Hapoalim.
MAARIV
- Meeting possible between Netanyahu and Arafat.
- Israel in secret decision to cancel oil drilling concessions in Golan Heights.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Conciliation between Levy and Netanyahu.
- Dollar down in sudden turnabout.
GLOBES
- Arison group bought 30 percent of Eurocom Communications shares for $20 to $30 million.
- Shapira recievers preparing 500 million shekel suit against Bank Hapoalim and Bank Leumi.
- Shamrock in negotiations with Bank Leumi over breaking up Koor Industries.
